title: Greedy Safe Choice
summary: Commit to a locally preferred option only when an argument shows that some optimal solution can begin with that choice without losing the global objective.
recognition_signals: the algorithm wants to make an irreversible local choice
a proof or exchange argument can show the local choice preserves an optimal solution
core_rules: Do not trust a greedy rule from intuition or a few examples; establish why the local choice is safe.
If changing the objective breaks the safety argument, the greedy rule no longer applies.
structural_steps: justify why an optimal solution can use that choice

common_confusions.distinction: Greedy commits to one locally safe path. Dynamic programming keeps multiple future trade-offs when no single local choice is provably safe.
Interval merging combines overlapping coverage; greedy interval scheduling selects a compatible subset to optimize an objective.
